title: Seeing Through Color Blindness: Social Networks as a Mechanism for Discrimination
abstract: arXiv:2006.15988v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: I study labor markets in which firms both hire via referrals and are race blind or color-blind. I develop an employment model showing that despite initial equality in ability, employment, wages, and network structure, minorities receive disproportionately fewer jobs through referrals and lower expected wages, simply because their social group is smaller. This discriminatory outcome, which I term "social network discrimination," arises from homophily and falls outside the dominant economics discrimination models, which are taste based and statistical. I calibrate the model using a nationally representative sample of youth networks to estimate the lower bound welfare gap caused by social network discrimination, which also disadvantages black workers. This paper isolates a potential underlying mechanism for inequality, adding to the understanding of labor-market disparities that have been widely studied across the social sciences. In do

translated_title: 看穿色盲：社会网络作为歧视的一种机制
translated_abstract: 我研究了企业既通过熟人推荐招聘又保持“种族色盲”（即不存在种族偏见）的劳动力市场。我建立了一个就业模型，表明尽管在能力、就业、工资和网络结构方面初始条件完全平等，少数族裔通过推荐获得的工作却不成比例地更少，预期工资也更低，而这仅仅是因为他们的社会群体规模较小。我将这种歧视性结果称为“社会网络歧视”，它源于同质性偏好，超出了主流经济学歧视模型（即基于偏好的歧视和统计性歧视）的解释范畴。我使用具有全国代表性的青年社会网络样本对模型进行校准，以估计社会网络歧视所造成的福利差距的下限，这种歧视同样不利于黑人劳动者。本文分离出一种潜在的深层不平等机制，加深了对社会科学领域广泛研究的劳动力市场差距问题的理解。
tldr: 本文提出“社会网络歧视”这一新机制：即使企业完全不带种族偏见，仅因少数族裔的社会网络规模较小且存在同质性偏好，他们也会在推荐就业中获得更少的工作机会和更低的预期工资。
